title: Redundant pumps
goals: Use AND and OR gates and see what redundancy buys.
See that the same events give different answers under different logic.
assumptions: Pumps P1 and P2 fail independently, each with a made-up probability of 0.1. Nothing here describes a real plant.

steps.prompt: Add two basic events, P1 and P2, each with probability 0.1.
steps.hint: Either pump alone can supply the flow, so both must fail to lose it.

steps.prompt: Add a gate "No coolant flow" that is true only when P1 AND P2 both fail. Make it the top event and run.
steps.hint: An AND gate fails only when every input fails.

steps.prompt: Now suppose either pump failing stops the flow. Change the gate to OR and run again.
steps.hint: Select the gate and change its type in the properties panel. An OR gate fails when any input fails.

mistakes.message: A probability above 1 is not allowed. Write 10 percent as 0.1.
A gate with one input only repeats that input. Give the gate both pumps.
One of your events is not connected to any gate, so it does not change the result.

hand_calculation: AND: both fail, so multiply. 0.1 x 0.1 = 0.01. One cut set of order 2: {P1, P2}.
OR: at least one fails, so 1 - (1 - 0.1)^2 = 1 - 0.81 = 0.19. Two cut sets of order 1: {P1}, {P2}.
Same two events, different logic, different answer.
